headline: Blind Advocate Challenges Maui County on Accessibility Gaps

meeting.body: Blind Advocate Challenges Maui County on Accessibility Gaps
meeting.summary: The commission heard a talk on blindness and voted to explore a list of accessibility problems reported by the public.
meeting.recap: The commission approved the minutes of its June 10, 2026 meeting.[[0:03:06]] A presenter who is legally blind gave a talk on blindness, accessibility and resources.[[0:03:28]] He said no agency on Maui helps blind people learn to live on their own.[[0:13:25]] He asked the commission to check whether county restrooms, elevators and crosswalks work for blind people.[[0:23:28]] The commission voted 5-0 to explore making a list of accessibility problems reported by the public.[[0:59:59]] The commission approved a draft letter about accessibility at a fair.[[1:03:57]] The commission tabled, or put off, a proposed housing development item until the next meeting.[[1:07:46]] Staff said a new grant funds home-delivered meals for people not eligible for Meals on Wheels.[[1:09:11]] Staff said three open office positions are waiting to be posted for hiring.[[1:10:17]] Staff reported helping a woman in her 80s who may have been a victim of contractor fraud.[[1:15:10]] A commissioner asked to discuss giving people with disabilities a seat on every commission.[[1:26:15]] The next meeting is August 13, 2026, at 12:30 p.m.[[1:27:21]]
decided: motion to approve the draft letter: The commission approved the draft letter about accessibility at a fair as written.
meeting.next: County officials will send the commission a response letter, but no date was given. A commissioner asked to follow up on the accessibility list at a future meeting. The housing development item will come back when the chair returns. Staff hope to finish hiring for the three positions within the next two months.

moments.q: Blindness is usually defined as having a visual acuity of 20 over 200 with correction.
there is no agency, no one here on Maui that helps blind individuals to live independently.
Public testimony from someone who took the presenter's blindness training
Staff suggests the commission host a walk audit of county facilities
five in favor and zero opposed. The motion passes.
